messages.author: 99a1cfc66539313c
messages.subject: Re: Why error in this plot?
parts:
Hi,

I think your main problem is that you are using "reserved" R keywords
as variable names. In particular, you are using "factor" as a name in
your dataframe.

I have modified your example so that the variable "factor" is now
called "variable", and then your code works.

You can also get rid of the warning about stacking being ill-defined,
by adding position="identity" to the geom definition.

Andrie

--

f <-
structure(list(Year = c(1940L, 1941L, 1942L, 1943L, 1944L, 1945L,
1946L, 1947L, 1948L, 1949L, 1940L, 1941L, 1942L, 1943L, 1944L,
1945L, 1946L, 1947L, 1948L, 1949L), variable = structure(c(2L,
2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,
1L, 1L, 1L), .Label = c("Real Deficit", "Real Surplus"), class =
"factor"),
value = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 40.2, 111.5, 5.7, -36.3, -59.1,
-219.1, -531.7, -501.1, -525.4, -175.9, 0, 0, 0)), .Names =
c("Year",
"variable", "value"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA,
-20L))

p <- ggplot(f,aes(Year,value))
p <- p + geom_bar(aes(colour=variable,fill=variable),stat="identity",
position="identity")

parts:
Hi:

Actually, the colour aesthetic is unnecessary in this example - fill is sufficient:

p <- ggplot(f,aes(Year,value, fill = variable))
p <- p + geom_bar(aes(fill=variable),stat="identity",
    position="identity")
p + scale_fill_manual(name="Legend",

It also removes the blue shadow at the top of the red bars when colour is included as an aesthetic.

BTW, Andrie, thanks for providing the data with dput() - much appreciated!!

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 99a1cfc66539313c
messages.subject: Re: Why error in this plot?
parts:
Dennis

Yes, I agree. In addition, I think it is better to let ggplot do the
colour conversion, by mapping fill to the original data, rather than
an artificially constructed vector in the data frame.

In the example below I use cast to recover the "original" economic
data into a single variable. I then map value to a
scale_fill_manual() scale. The trick is to use sign() to determine
whether the data is positive or negative, and then factor() to convert
this into a discrete value.

Andrie

--

library(reshape)

f <-
structure(list(Year = c(1940L, 1941L, 1942L, 1943L, 1944L, 1945L,
1946L, 1947L, 1948L, 1949L, 1940L, 1941L, 1942L, 1943L, 1944L,
1945L, 1946L, 1947L, 1948L, 1949L), variable = structure(c(2L,
2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,
1L, 1L, 1L), .Label = c("Real Deficit", "Real Surplus"), class =
"factor"),
value = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 40.2, 111.5, 5.7, -36.3, -59.1,
-219.1, -531.7, -501.1, -525.4, -175.9, 0, 0, 0)), .Names =
c("Year",
"variable", "value"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA,
-20L))

castf <- as.data.frame(cast(f, Year~variable))
g <- data.frame(Year=castf$Year,
value=(castf$`Real Surplus` + castf$`Real Deficit`))


p <- ggplot(g, aes(x=Year, y=value, fill=factor(sign(value))))
p <- p + geom_bar(stat="identity", position="identity")
p <- p + scale_fill_manual(name="GDP",
breaks=c(-1,1),
values=c("red", "blue"),
labels=c("Deficit", "Surplus"))
p
